title: E-Math algebra: expansion, factorisation and changing the subject
subject: math

steps.text: Find the highest common factor of 6x and 9: HCF = 3.
steps.annotation: Both terms are multiples of 3, and no larger factor is shared.
This gives the terms that will sit inside the bracket.
The HCF goes outside the bracket; expanding 3(2x + 3) returns 6x + 9, which checks the answer.

complete.selfExplanation: Explain how expanding your answer proves the factorisation is correct.

steps.annotation: Multiply every term inside the bracket by 2.
Only terms in the same variable can be combined.
The constant term 6 is unchanged by collecting the x terms.

faded.selfExplanation: The first step is shown. Say which terms you would combine next and why they can be combined.

paired.problem: Make x the subject of y = 3x + 5.
paired.solution: Subtract 5 from both sides: y - 5 = 3x. Divide both sides by 3: x = (y - 5) / 3. Each step reverses one operation applied to x, in reverse order.
